question: What will be the average daily mean temperature in Sydney over the 7 days ending October 18, 2026, in degrees Celsius?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the mean of the daily mean 2-metre air temperatures from 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 at latitude -33.87, longitude 151.21 (Sydney), from the ERA5 reanalysis as served by the Open-Meteo historical weather API (archive-api.open-meteo.com), in degrees Celsius.
research:
I couldn't get any forecast or market specific to 12-18 October 2026. The best evidence is past ERA5 values for the same week, which have run from about 15.9 to 20.3°C in recent years, and an official outlook favouring above-average spring temperatures.

## 1. Resolution source
- I queried the Open-Meteo ERA5 archive (archive-api.open-meteo.com) for -33.87, 151.21, daily `temperature_2m_mean`. For 2022-2026 I left the timezone at its default (GMT); the 2021 query used Australia/Sydney time. [Open-Meteo archive](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.87&longitude=151.21&start_date=2026-09-01&end_date=2026-10-04&daily=temperature_2m_mean)
- 2026-10-04: the latest value shown is 17.6°C. The days before it: 1 Oct 21.4, 2 Oct 19.8, 3 Oct 17.4. Values from the last few days may be preliminary and could be revised.
- The question doesn't say which timezone it uses. The choice can move a daily mean by a few tenths of a degree.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing is settled. The 12-18 October window hasn't started, and no part of it is known yet.

## 3. Recent news
- 2026-10-01 and 2026-09-24: the Bureau of Meteorology (BoM) issued outlooks for October to January. Both pages returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't read them. [BoM 1 Oct](https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/ahead/outlooks/archive/20261001-outlook.shtml), [BoM 24 Sep](https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/ahead/outlooks/archive/20260924-outlook.shtml)
- 2026-09-17: the BoM outlook for October to January (as summarised in search results) says above-average temperatures are likely across much of Australia for the rest of 2026. It also warns that El Niño is only one factor. [BoM](https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/ahead/outlooks/archive/20260917-outlook.shtml)
- 2026-08-27: BoM's spring long-range forecast says above-average temperatures are likely across most of Australia, with a higher risk of early-season heat, and El Niño expected to strengthen and persist. [BoM](https://www.bom.gov.au/news-and-media/the-bureau-issues-long-range-forecast-for-spring)
- 2026 (June): El Niño was declared to be underway. For Sydney, forecasts pointed to below-average rain and above-average temperatures. [Time Out](https://www.timeout.com/sydney/news/el-nino-is-officially-underway-heres-what-that-means-for-sydneys-weather-forecast-061826)

## 4. Base rates
ERA5 means for 12-18 October, from the Open-Meteo archive:
- 2021: 15.9°C (Sydney time). Daily range 14.8-17.8. [2021](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.87&longitude=151.21&start_date=2021-10-01&end_date=2021-10-20&daily=temperature_2m_mean&timezone=Australia/Sydney)
- 2022: 16.8°C. Daily range 15.6-17.7. [2022](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.87&longitude=151.21&start_date=2022-09-20&end_date=2022-10-20&daily=temperature_2m_mean)
- 2023: 17.8°C. Daily range 15.9-21.2. This was an El Niño year. [2023](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.87&longitude=151.21&start_date=2023-09-20&end_date=2023-10-20&daily=temperature_2m_mean)
- 2024: 16.7°C. Daily range 13.8-20.7. [2024](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.87&longitude=151.21&start_date=2024-09-20&end_date=2024-10-20&daily=temperature_2m_mean)
- 2025: 20.3°C. Daily range 17.0-23.8. [2025](https://archive-api.open-meteo.com/v1/archive?latitude=-33.87&longitude=151.21&start_date=2025-09-20&end_date=2025-10-20&daily=temperature_2m_mean)
- The 5-year mean is about 17.5°C, and 17.9°C for 2022-2025 only. The spread is roughly 15.9-20.3, a standard deviation of about 1.6°C. Single days in this window range from 13.8 to 23.8°C.

**Seasonal path, 1-4 Oct mean compared with 12-18 Oct mean:**
- 2022: 14.1 → 16.8 (+2.7)
- 2023: 22.1 → 17.8 (-4.3)
- 2024: 15.9 → 16.7 (+0.8)
- 2025: 17.9 → 20.3 (+2.4)
- 2026: 1-4 October averages 19.1°C. That is above 2022, 2024 and 2025 but below 2023, so this year is running warm. The early-October value has not reliably predicted the mid-October week.
- September 2026 averaged about 17.3°C, with frequent swings between 12.8 and 24.6°C.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold markets, and no expert forecast specific to this week or quantity.

## 6. Upcoming events and forecasts
- The latest official guidance I could find favours above-average spring temperatures in an El Niño year: BoM's 17 September summary and the August spring outlook. I couldn't read the BoM outlooks dated 24 September and 1 October (403 errors).
- I couldn't get a 7-16 day forecast for 12-18 October issued on or before 4 October. The data I saw for that period came from after the cutoff, so I ignored it.
- Things that could move the outcome include warm north-westerly days ahead of fronts (2025 had several days around 24°C) and cool southerly changes or onshore patterns (single days of 13-15°C).
